series.$note: series.observed holds several sources and must not be read as one curve. DS-35: All greenhouse gases including land-use change, GWP100 (OWID, from Climate Watch / PIK), from 1990. DS-02: Asset-level observed emissions, CO₂e GWP100 (Climate TRACE); land use accounted differently from OWID, 2015-2025. DS-40: Total GHG emissions including LULUCF/LUCF exactly as the Party submitted them to the UNFCCC, on that Party’s own reporting guidelines and GWP set (UNFCCC Data Interface, snapshot of 2024-07-05). Non-Annex I Parties report only the years their national communications cover, and the figure is negative where reported removals exceed reported emissions. Points from an NDC document are that document's own inventory basis. The same year can appear more than once with different values; R3 keeps them side by side and never averages them.

derived.$reason: 35 observed years are loaded, but no NDC target emissions figure has been parsed, so there is nothing to measure the trend against.

country_profile.$note: Population is World Bank SP.POP.TOTL for the latest year published in the 2015–2025 window. Income group is the World Bank's own classification, not a UNFCCC one.

ndc_registry.$note: The registry states which submission is current and where it is. It carries no target figure, so nothing in ndc.* is derived from it.

ndc_assessment.vintage: First (I)NDC round, as assessed by WRI CAIT (2016). Not the latest submission.
ndc_assessment.summary: "Ecuador intends to reduce its emissions in the energy sector in 20.4-25% below the BAU scenario. However, a potential for reducing emissions even further in the energy sector, to a level between 37.5 and 45.8% with respect to the BAU baseline has also been calculated. This potential could be harnessed in light of the appropriate circumstances in terms of availability of resources and support offered by the international community. This is a second scenario dependent upon international support and will translate into a per capita emissions reduction in 2025 of 40% below the BAU levels."
ndc_assessment.ghg_target: 20.4-25% (unconditional) to 37.5-45.8% (conditional) reduction in emissions in the energy sector by 2025 compared to the BAU scenario, equivalent to 40% reduction (conditional) in emissions per capita by 2025 compared to the BAU levels.
ndc_assessment.gases: CO2, CH4; NO2, CO, PM, N2O, SO2
ndc_assessment.$note: Third-party assessment of the first (I)NDC round. It is not merged into ndc.*, is not used by derive(), and does not appear on the dial as a target.

ndc_document.$reason: no sentence in this document states an economy-wide percentage reduction against a base year or a business-as-usual projection.

verdict.text: The registry's current submission for this Party is Second NDC, filed 2025-02-06. 52 observed values are loaded from DS-02 (11), DS-35 (35), DS-40 (6). For 2024 the sources disagree: DS-02 89.5 MtCO₂e, DS-35 63.1 MtCO₂e. They are on different inventory scopes and the engine does not reconcile them. No implementation gap is reported: 35 observed years are loaded, but no NDC target emissions figure has been parsed, so there is nothing to measure the trend against. It submitted BTR1. 3 of 8 components have been confirmed in the document; the rest are unparsed, which is not a finding against the country. ND-GAIN scores it 43.6 for 2024. In the first NDC round, WRI's CAIT assessment recorded: 20.4-25% (unconditional) to 37.5-45.8% (conditional) reduction in emissions in the energy sector by 2025 compared to the BAU scenario, equivalent to 40% reduction (conditional) in emissions per capita by 2025 compared to the BAU levels. It was classed both. That is a 2016 assessment of an earlier submission, not the target above. Projected warming for 2080-2099 against 1995-2014 ranges from +1.03°C under SSP1-2.6 to +4°C under SSP5-8.5. These are model runs, not observations.
